plan: [ Second-price sealed-bid auction: best to bid my true private value. With a single round and no opportunity to learn, bidding 29 maximizes expected payoff — if I win I pay the second-highest bid, so bidding my true value yields positive surplus whenever it’s profitable. Submit bid = 29. ]

[I treat this as a second-price (Vickrey) auction: bidding your true private value maximizes expected surplus in the standard case and avoids over- or underbidding when signals are symmetric. With one round and no learning, shading is unlikely to help because others’ bids only inform about the common component I can't observe. My private value is $17, so I bid that (in $0.1 increments) to capture any positive surplus if I win while avoiding systematic loss.]

[My value is 34. Given v = C + t with t∈[0,20], C’s posterior is uniform on [14,29], so E[C|v]=21.5. Expected opponent signal = E[C|v]+E[t]=21.5+10=31.5. Because signals are affiliated (winner’s curse risk), I will shade below my private value rather than bid truthfully. I want to be slightly above opponents’ expected signals but leave positive surplus, so I bid modestly below 34 to balance win probability and profit.]
